subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should deep audit cap installed plugin manifests at 1 MiB even though larger valid manifests lose explicit forced scanning of declared hidden or `node_modules` entries?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but the threshold defines an owner-level threat-model tradeoff between bounded resource use and manifest-driven audit coverage.

options.title: Accept the 1 MiB policy
options.body: Keep the warning and normal root scan as the supported behavior for oversized manifests.

options.title: Preserve declared-entry coverage
options.body: Require a different bounded extraction strategy if all declared skipped-path entries must remain force-scanned.

recommendation.title: Accept the 1 MiB policy
recommendation.body: Keep the warning and normal root scan as the supported behavior for oversized manifests.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS identifies this team as the owner of the changed security boundary.
